## What this letter says
This letter is from a specialist to another doctor. You are getting a copy. It is about your plan to collect sperm (sperm harvesting).

- You had a vasectomy 10 years ago.
- You had a vasectomy reversal almost two years ago at the University of Michigan. It failed.
- You have had no sperm in your semen (azoospermic) since then.
- The operation note suggests some sperm and sperm head may have been present on the right side. This is possible, not certain.
- Your wife has had several tries at ovulation induction. They did not work. This seems to be because of some anatomic abnormality. This is not certain.
- You may want a fresh specimen harvest instead of cryopreservation. This is possible, not certain.
- In a recent phone call, you said you do not want sperm harvesting at all unless your wife's ovulation has been confirmed.

## What you need to do
1. The specialist has asked the other doctor to send the actual plan. Then the procedure can be arranged.
2. The letter does not give you any other tasks.

## Dates and medicines
- The letter does not list any medicines.
- The letter has a visit date and a harvesting date. Both are blank, so they cannot be given here.
- The harvesting date may change if a fresh specimen is needed.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does azoospermic mean for me?
- What is the difference between a fresh specimen harvest and cryopreservation?
- When will the plan for my wife's ovulation induction be ready?
- What is the date for my harvesting procedure?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*

problems.explanation_says: In a recent phone call, you said you do not want sperm harvesting at all unless your wife's ovulation has been confirmed.
problems.letter_says: I recently received a phone call suggesting that he does not want to do this at all unless his wife's ovulation has been confirmed.
problems.why: The letter says the call 'suggested' this. The explanation states it as a definite statement by the patient.

problems.explanation_says: You may want a fresh specimen harvest instead of cryopreservation. (No mention that cryopreservation was requested at the visit or that the harvest is planned before the next ovulation induction.)
problems.letter_says: At the time that he left the office, he was asking for cryopreservation... interested in sperm harvesting and cryopreservation prior to the next attempted ovulation induction.
problems.why: The explanation leaves out that the patient's original request was cryopreservation, and that the plan is timed before the next ovulation induction. Both help explain why the plan is uncertain.

verifier.summary: The explanation is mostly faithful. It has two minor problems: it states a phone call as certain when the letter only says it 'suggested' this, and it leaves out the original request for cryopreservation and the timing before the next ovulation induction.
